comment: My husband was sent home at eleven at night last winter because they needed the bed. If a computer starts saying how many must go home, that will happen more.
Who checks the person at home can cope? The forecast won't know my mother lives alone.
I waited 19 hours on a trolley. If this means beds are ready sooner I am for it.
My hip operation was cancelled twice on the morning. Tell me three days before, not after I have stopped eating.
Is this a private company being given our records? Who agreed to that? I do not remember being asked.
I opted out of my data being shared years ago. Does that count here?
Will the company sell what it learns from our hospital to other hospitals? Does the trust get anything back?
People who shout get beds. People like my neighbour who doesn't speak much English wait. Will the computer fix that or copy it?
My son has a learning disability. Every admission they have no idea he is coming. Does it plan for people like him?
When it is wrong, who do I complain to? The hospital will blame the software and the software people will blame the hospital.
I'd want the board to see how often it is wrong, every month, in public papers.
Just be honest. If it's a guess, say it's a guess.
The nurses are run ragged already. If this is about having fewer of them on quiet days, say so.
If it helps them plan so there's a bed on the right ward and not three wards in three days, good. I was moved at 2am twice.
I trust the sister on the ward. I don't know these people.
The people stuck in hospital waiting for care at home are the poorest and the oldest. A bed forecast doesn't build a single care package.
Fine by me as long as my name isn't on it.
Will patients be told this is being used? A poster at least.
What does it cost and what are we stopping doing to pay for it?
Anything that gets ambulances away from the door quicker. My wife waited two hours outside.
The last system they brought in lost my appointment. Forgive me if I'm not excited.
Discharge planning starts too late as it is. If this makes them start earlier, fine. If it makes them rush, no.
Nobody from the mental health service users' group is in this room. They wait longest of all in A&E.
Can a nurse say no to it? If she can't, it's the computer running the ward.
In June we carry children to the hospital and they lie three on a bed. If the hospital knew before, maybe they prepare.
Many organisations come with tablets. They count us, they leave. What stays?
Families pay cash. If the hospital spends money on computers and there are still no drugs, people will be angry.
Some illnesses people do not want known in the village. Who will see the registers?
During the strike mothers delivered at home. No computer helps when there are no nurses.
People from Ndere and Lakeshore cannot reach the hospital when the road is cut. They are not in your numbers.
It should be explained in Kiswahili and Dholuo at the baraza, not only to the doctors.
If it says prepare for 100 children and the county sends nothing, what then?
